stem: Why does the clinician start from a different legal presumption for the 18-year-old sibling than for the 17-year-old sibling?

options.text: Because adults are presumed competent to consent, whereas a minor’s competence must be determined rather than presumed
Because 18-year-olds can no longer refuse treatment
Because once a patient turns 18, consent from parents is always still required as backup
Because competence assessment is only relevant in emergencies for minors
Because a 17-year-old is automatically incompetent to make medical decisions

explanation: Adults are presumed competent to consent. In contrast, a minor’s competence must be assessed rather than presumed, so the legal starting point differs once the patient turns 18.

citations.source: Louisa Leone MD3 2025 - Child and Adolescent Health - Study Notes.pdf

optionExplanations.A: Correct because adults are presumed competent to consent, whereas a minor’s competence must be determined rather than presumed
optionExplanations.B: Incorrect because adults can still refuse treatment unless another legal basis overrides that decision
optionExplanations.C: Incorrect because parental consent is not always required for adults
optionExplanations.D: Incorrect because competence assessment is relevant whenever capacity or consent needs to be established, not only in emergencies
optionExplanations.E: Incorrect because a 17-year-old is not automatically incompetent; competence must be assessed
